note: The operators hub: where the city finds and grows the humans who operate and build its companies. It holds disciplines, seats, criteria and the process, never a real person's name, e-mail, CV or profile. The HQ joins it with each company's org, asks and parked roles, read through the company's own tools. tools/check.mjs validates it.

intake.how: Applications would go to a private intake that the founder chooses and runs, outside every public repository and every published snapshot. None exists yet: this registry has no form, no account and no address to write to.

disciplines.title: Engineering
disciplines.summary: Builds and keeps the code the agents ship: the product, its checks, the deploy path.
inAnAgentCompany: Approves each production deploy of a code company (P13), from the release the agents prepared and its checks
Owns the referee's harness when it is code: the test suite, the judge script, what 'main never gets worse' means
Reviews a critical change's readiness record (deploys, the event API, auth, user data) when no other engineer can
criteria: Lands a change past the company's referee with its predictions committed first
Says no to an unapproved deploy, every time
Leaves the next worker a handoff they can act on

disciplines.title: Applied science and research
disciplines.summary: Turns questions into claims that reproduce: predictions first, held-out data, an independent check.
inAnAgentCompany: Holds the referee and its held-out sets as evaluation steward (P13: the referee is a human seat); draws the seeds and splits the makers never see
Judges a run against the predictions committed before it, wrong ones included
Decides when a headline is withdrawn because it did not reproduce
criteria: Writes a prediction with a wrong-if and a tolerance before a run
Keeps a held-out set held out (never reads it as a maker)
Reports a wrong prediction as plainly as a right one

disciplines.title: Product
disciplines.summary: Decides what is worth building and why, and says no to the rest.
inAnAgentCompany: Approves the briefs agents build from (what and why), for a site feature or a new lesson line
Answers the asks that wait on the owner: priorities, scope, which option
Approves the org design (P13): an org only for a reason the work gives, few members
criteria: Turns an ask into a decision record with its options and objections
Cuts scope to fit a cost target with a stop rule
Can say which principle a design breaks and why

disciplines.title: Operations and infrastructure
disciplines.summary: Keeps every company's infrastructure boring: deploys, budgets, CI, spend, hygiene.
inAnAgentCompany: Approves budgets and each spend line (P13), and pauses work over twice its cost target
Approves each deploy, preview or production, after seeing what will ship
Owns incidents' correction-of-error actions and the drills that test the runbooks
criteria: Approves or refuses a prepared deploy from its evidence, not its description
Reads a spend ledger and stops a run at its stop rule
Runs a drill without seeing its answers first

disciplines.title: Editorial
disciplines.summary: Keeps the voice the author's: every edit a proposal, every fact checked by someone else.
inAnAgentCompany: Accepts, declines or rewrites each proposed edit as the author (the baseline text changes only with the author's yes)
Spot-checks translations and decides on a new locale
Approves each release of a book or a post, recorded with the author's words
criteria: Decides on a blind sample of edits before reading the editor's account
Keeps objections with the decision when overriding an editor
Never lets a fact through that its own writer checked

disciplines.title: Design
disciplines.summary: Makes the work legible: art, covers, interfaces, logos, at phone width and in the dark.
inAnAgentCompany: Commissions and accepts art and covers (the agents prepare briefs; a human accepts the result)
Owns a company's visual standard: its design system, its logo, its accessibility bar
Judges interfaces as a user would, artifact before account
criteria: Accepts or rejects a design against acceptance checks written before it was drawn
Checks light and dark and a 390-pixel phone before saying yes
Knows what may not be copied (trademarks, existing characters)

disciplines.title: Growth
disciplines.summary: Finds the readers, learners and users, without buying them or misleading them.
inAnAgentCompany: Approves a launch or publication plan with a date (the agents draft it)
Decides what is shared publicly, and when, including city news and newsletters
Owns the experiments that measure reach, with predictions first
criteria: Writes a launch's predictions before it goes out, and reads them after
Never publishes a claim the referee has not passed
Keeps personal data out of every public channel

founder.title: Owner (CEO)
founder.what: approves every deploy, every spend and the org design; answers the asks that wait on the owner

evaluation-steward.title: Evaluation steward
evaluation-steward.what: owns the referee and its held-out sets; draws what the makers never see

seats.title: Evaluation steward (holds the drill set)
seats.what: holds the held-out drill set of seeded faults outside the repository and judges each milestone against it

seats.title: Evaluation steward (holds the held-out seeds and splits)
seats.what: draws the seeds, splits and scenarios each claim is reproduced on, and keeps them outside every repository

seats.title: Evaluation steward (the blind sample)
seats.what: draws the blind sample of edits the founder decides on before reading the writer's account

seats.title: Author (accepts, declines or rewrites every edit)
seats.what: the voice is the author's: every edit is a proposal; each release is approved with the author's words

seats.title: Author (approves posts, spot-checks translations, approves deploys)
seats.what: writes and decides; edits are proposals; each deploy needs the author's approval

seats.title: Founder approvals (deploys and launches)
seats.what: approves each deploy and each lesson launch; ratifies constitutional amendments

seats.title: Owner approvals (production deploys)
seats.what: approves each production deploy of the web app and records it in its release log

seats.title: Referee owner (the hidden score)
seats.what: keeps the hidden part of SQLite's own tests the engine is judged on; approves spending

seats.title: Referee owner (correct before fast)
seats.what: keeps the referee that compiles Lua and SQLite; approves spending and deploys

seats.title: City founder (org designs and the platform's deploys)
seats.what: approves every company's org design and every city HQ deploy

process.title: How the city judges a human operator
process.summary: The same principles as for agents: a real task, a referee chosen before the work, predictions first, a cost target with a stop rule, and a check by someone other than the candidate.
steps: Pick a seat and a trial task the seat really does (approve or refuse a prepared deploy; decide a blind sample of edits; judge a run against its predictions; set a budget line and a stop rule).
Write the referee before the trial: what a good outcome is, measured how, by whom. The candidate sees the task, not the answers.
The candidate commits predictions first: what they expect, and what would show them wrong.
Set a cost target (hours) with a stop rule; work over twice the target stops and is reviewed.
Run the trial on a held-out case the candidate has not seen, inside a sandbox with no production access and no secrets.
Someone other than the candidate checks the result against the referee, artifact before account, and writes it up with its objections.
The founder decides, as with any seat change (P13), in a decision record kept in the private intake, not in a public repository.
never: No trial touches production, real users' data or a secret
No personal data in any repository or snapshot: names, e-mails, CVs and results stay in the founder's private intake
No unpaid production work disguised as a trial

training.title: Operators Academy
training.where: system3-meta academy/ (a city app; design note docs/proposals/2026-10-26-operators-academy.md)
training.what: Drills from the city's own records, as predict, explore and reveal cards, in tracks that match the disciplines: common core, engineering, applied science, product, operations and infrastructure, editorial. Each track has a held-out drill, and the pass marks were fixed before anyone took one.
training.note: Practice for a seat and its trial, not a substitute for it. Its certificate is a summary of a viewer's own progress, kept in their browser: not a credential, and not seen by the city.

profile.note: The shape an operator's profile would take inside the private intake. Only the fictional example below is published; real profiles never are.

schema.id: a handle chosen by the intake, never a real name
schema.seats: the seat kinds they would fill (e.g. deploy approver, evaluation steward)
schema.trials: [{ seat, task, predictions, referee, result: passed|failed|withdrawn, checkedBy: a role }]
schema.growth: what they want to learn next, as a discipline and a seat
schema.consent: what of this they agreed to share, and with whom

example.label: A fictional operator, to show the shape. Not a real person.

trials.task: approve or refuse three prepared deploys, one of them seeded with a failing check
trials.predictions: refuses the seeded one; approves two within 10 minutes each
trials.referee: the seeded fault list, held by the evaluation steward

example.growth: applied-science: hold a held-out set for one milestone
